To start August, ongoing drought conditions in Sheridan County were at (D2-Severe), with the exception of the extreme southwest portion of Sheridan County which remained in (D3-Extreme) drought.  On the third week of August, (D3-Extreme) expanded into southern and western areas of Sheridan county, while the northeastern half of Sheridan county remained in (D2-Severe).  These conditions continued through the remainder of the month.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions in Daniels County were at (D2-Severe) in all but the southeastern areas and far western tip of the county, which were in (D3-Extreme) drought.  During the third week of August, the entire county worsened to (D3-Extreme) conditions. At the end of the month the western third of Daniels County worsened to (D4-Exceptional) conditions while the eastern two thirds of the county remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start the month of August, ongoing drought conditions (D3-Extreme) were in place across the western and southeastern part of Eastern Roosevelt County, while the northeastern part of Eastern Roosevelt county remained in (D2-Severe) drought.  By the third week all of Eastern Roosevelt County was in (D3-Extreme) drought.  By the end of August, the far southwestern corner had worsened to (D4-Exceptional) drought while the rest of the county remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions (D3-Extreme) covered most of Richland County with the exception of the far southeastern corner which was in (D2-Severe) drought.  By the end of the month, the northwestern two thirds of Richland County had worsened to (D4 Exceptional) with the far southeastern corner remaining in (D2-Severe) and the rest of eastern Richland County remaining in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start August, all of Dawson County was in (D3-Extreme) drought conditions.  By the third week of August, the far southern edge of Dawson County worsened to (D4-Exceptional) drought conditions.  By the end of the month, all but the far eastern edge of Dawson County had worsened to (D4-Exceptional) conditions, that area remained in (D3-Extreme) drought.

To start the month of August, all but the extreme northeast corner of Wibaux County was in (D3-Extreme) drought conditions with the extreme northeast corner being in (D2-Severe) drought.  On the third week of August, the southern two thirds of Wibaux County worsened to (D4-Exceptional) conditions.  The northeastern corner remained in (D2-Severe) conditions and the rest of the northern part of Wibaux County remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  These conditions remained the same through the end of the month.

To start the month of August, ongoing drought conditions (D3-Extreme) covered all of Prairie County.  On the third week, the eastern half of Prairie County worsened to (D4-Exceptional) while the western half remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  At the end of the month (D4-Exceptional) expanded further west to cover the eastern two thirds of Prairie County, with the western third remaining in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions (D3-Extreme) continued for all but the northwestern corner of western Roosevelt County where this area had (D2-Severe) conditions.  By the third week of August, all of western Roosevelt County was in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  By the end of August (D4-Exceptional) conditions had expanded into the southwestern area, where the rest of western Roosevelt county remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions for McCone County worsened (D3-Extreme) for the majority of the county, the exception being the far northwestern corner where (D4-Exceptional) conditions were occurring.  By the end of the month, all but the southeastern corner of McCone County was in (D4-Exceptional) with the southeastern corner remaining in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions (D3-Extreme) occurred across most of Northern Valley County, the exception being (D2-Severe) in the far southeast corner of Northern Valley County.  By the third week of August, all of Northern Valley County was in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  By the end of the month, the eastern half of Northern Valley County had worsened to (D4-Exceptional) while the western half remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start the month of August, ongoing drought conditions (D4-Exceptional) were found in the western two thirds of Central and Southern Valley County.  Most of the eastern third was in (D3-Extreme) conditions, with the exception of the far northeast corner which was in (D2-Severe) conditions.  By the third week all of the eastern third of Central and Southern Valley County worsened to (D3-Extreme) conditions, while the western two thirds remained in (D4-Exceptional) drought.  At the end of the month, all but a little area of the north central portion of Central and Southern Valley County had worsened to (D4-Exceptional) conditions while that little portion remained in (D3-Extreme) drought.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions were in (D4-Exceptional) conditions across the northwestern third of Garfield County with the southeastern two thirds of Garfield County in (D3-Extreme) drought. At the end of August an area around the Dry Creek Arm of Fort Peck Lake worsened to (D4-Exceptional) conditions while the southeastern two thirds of Garfield County remained in (D3-Extreme) drought.

To start the month of August, ongoing drought conditions started at (D3-Extreme) for all but the extreme northwest corner of Northern Phillips county which remained in (D2-Severe).  These conditions remained the same through the end of August.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions were (D4-Exceptional) in the eastern and southeastern three quarters of Central and Southeast Phillips County, with the western and north western quarter in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  These conditions remained the same through the end of August.

To start August, ongoing drought conditions were (D4-Exceptional) for the northern three quarters of Petroleum County, while the southern quarter of Petroleum County remained in (D3-Extreme) conditions.  These conditions remained the same through the end of August.
To start August, ongoing drought conditions were in (D3-Extreme) conditions for all of the Little Rocky Mountains.  These conditions remained the same through the end of August.

To start January, all of Western Roosevelt County was in (D3-Extreme) drought conditions. This would continue through the end of January.
To start January, ongoing drought conditions in all of McCone County was at (D3-Extreme) conditions.  These conditions would remain the same through the end of January.

To start January, ongoing drought conditions in all of Northern Valley County were at (D3-Extreme) drought conditions.  During the last week of January all but the southeastern corner of the county improved to (D2-Severe) conditions, with the southeastern corner remaining in (D3-Extreme) conditions.

To start January, ongoing drought conditions in all of Central and Southern Valley County was in (D3-Extreme) drought. Southeast Garfield County was in (D2-Severe) drought at the beginning of January.  These conditions would remain the same through the end of January.

To start January, all of Central and Southeast Phillips County improved to (D3-Extreme) drought conditions.  By the last week of January, the northeastern third of Central and Southeast Phillips County improved to (D2-Severe) drought.  The northwestern corner and the southern half of the area would remain in (D3-Extreme) drought.  These conditions lasted through the end of January.
